key_insight: In coronene, SevenNet increasingly underestimates vacancy formation energies as edge under-coordination grows, while closely matching mean Stone–Wales energies.
engineering_relevance: SevenNet can support rapid graphene quantum-dot structure screening and preliminary ranking, but absolute vacancy energies require DFT validation.
method: Benchmark SevenNet (7net-omni-i12) against spin-polarized PBE DFT in GPAW for coronene (C24H12).
Evaluate monovacancy, divacancy, and Stone–Wales defect landscapes.
Compare 28 matched vacancy and divacancy reconstructions using self-consistent chemical-potential reservoirs.
evidence_signal: SevenNet underestimates all 28 matched vacancy/divacancy formation energies, with mean deficits rising across edge C–H bond-breaking classes from 0.30 to 0.74 eV for monovacancies and 0.65 to 1.11 eV for divacancies; mean Stone–Wales energies differ by only 0.013 eV.
watch_item: These results are specific to coronene; multi-basin edge reconstructions warrant DFT checks, with symmetry-equivalent energy spreads serving as a relaxation diagnostic.
paper_title: Edge-scaling softening of a universal machine-learned potential: point-defect formation energies in a coronene graphene quantum dot
